Rendering large landscapes

Wide Views Demo

A synthetic enterprise: 4 portfolios, 30 applications, 90 interfaces, services and records, 12 capabilities, 42 flows. Every view below is a real LikeC4 view laid out by Graphviz dot, with the measured size of its layout. Click a view to open it full screen; click an element to drill down where a sub-view exists.

Problem1 Nest2 Drill down3 Show less4 Grid instead5 FrameSummary

!The problem: a flat landscape

dot puts every element without a parent on one row per rank. Thirty applications and twelve capabilities, included flat, give two rows: one is 9,300 px wide. In a page frame the view is scaled to 12 %, and the labels disappear.

view v0_apps {
  include credit.** where kind is application-component
  include payments.** where kind is application-component
  include platform.** where kind is application-component
  include risk.** where kind is application-component
  include cap.** where kind is capability
  exclude * -> * where kind is flow
  autoLayout TopBottom 40 60
}
✕Two ranks, 30 nodes on the second one. Nothing is wrong with the model: the view has no structure to wrap on.

Layout 9,306 × 496 px · 47 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.12

Variant: everything, even nested

Including the 90 interfaces, services and records as well keeps the parents, so the view is no longer a strip, but 124 nodes make it 5,000 × 3,300 px. Readable only zoomed in; useless as an overview.

Layout 5,085 × 3,344 px · 124 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.17

1Nest, so the layout has something to wrap

Include the portfolios as well as their applications. dot lays out each portfolio as a compound block and stacks the blocks. Same 30 applications, 4 × less wide.

view v1_nested {
  include credit, payments, platform, risk, credit.*, payments.*, platform.*, risk.*
  exclude * -> * where kind is flow
  autoLayout TopBottom 32 48
}
✓From 9,300 × 500 to 2,300 × 2,100 px: a rectangle that fits a frame at 26 % instead of 12 %, and reads at a glance once opened. The capability edges are aggregated on the collapsed applications.

Layout 2,308 × 2,130 px · 34 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.26

1b · The same with view-level groups

When the model has no parent to include (or you want another grouping than the model's), group blocks in the view do the same thing without changing the elements. Useful for a view grouped by team, by hosting zone or by lifecycle.

view v1_groups {
  group 'Corporate credit' {
    include credit.*
  }
  group 'Payments' {
    include payments.*
  }
  group 'Delivery platform' {
    include platform.*
  }
  group 'Risk & finance' {
    include risk.*
  }
  exclude * -> * where kind is flow
  autoLayout TopBottom 32 48
}
✓Same proportions as 1. Groups are view-only: no new element, no id, nothing for the validator.

Layout 2,436 × 2,471 px · 38 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.23

2Drill down instead of showing everything

Three levels, each one a view of about 10 to 15 nodes: the enterprise (portfolios and capability map), a portfolio (its applications and the capabilities they realize), an application (its interface, service, record and the applications it exchanges with). A view … of <element> becomes the element's default drill-down: click a portfolio, then an application.

L0Enterprise

Layout 1,200 × 1,068 px · 9 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.52

L1Portfolio · Corporate credit

Layout 3,120 × 496 px · 15 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.35

L2Application · Facility

Layout 1,276 × 946 px · 10 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.59

view v2_enterprise {
  include credit, payments, platform, risk, cap, cap.*
  autoLayout TopBottom 32 48
}
view v2_credit of credit {
  include *, cap.lend.*
  exclude * -> * where kind is flow
  autoLayout TopBottom 32 48
}
view v2_credit_facility of credit.facility {
  include *, -> * ->
  autoLayout TopBottom 32 48
}
✓Every view fits a frame at 35 % or better and reads without zooming. The portfolio view is still 3,100 px wide with 8 applications on one row: nest again (by team, by value stream) when a portfolio grows past about 10 applications.

Catalogue tables, not views, are where the full list of 30 applications belongs. A view with more than about 40 nodes is not read, whatever the layout.

3Show less per view

One kind of element (application components), no flows, size xs, tighter spacing. Combined with nesting this is the densest overview that still reads: 30 applications in 1,900 × 1,700 px.

view v3_reduced {
  include credit, payments, platform, risk
  include credit.** where kind is application-component
  include payments.** where kind is application-component
  include platform.** where kind is application-component
  include risk.** where kind is application-component
  exclude * -> * where kind is flow
  style * { size xs }
  autoLayout TopBottom 20 32
}
✓Reduction alone does not fix a strip: 30 small boxes on one row are still 4,500 px wide. It works on top of 1 or 2.

Layout 1,866 × 1,673 px · 34 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.33

4A grid for matrix-shaped views

A capability map, an application × capability matrix or a landscape per layer is a grid, not a graph. Generated from the same model (bb.json) as a CSS grid of ArchiMate figures, it wraps to the window width, stays readable on a phone and needs no layout engine. LikeC4 keeps the views that have relationships to show.

5Rendering: give the frame a real height

The web component fits the view to its container. A 220 px frame shrinks the nested landscape to 10 %; a frame of 60 to 80 % of the viewport shows it at 26 %, with every label legible. Keep browser on the component so one click opens the view full screen, with zoom and the element panel.

220 px frame

Layout 2,308 × 2,130 px · 34 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.26

.lc4-frame { height: 220px; }

clamp(480px, 78vh, 900px)

Layout 2,308 × 2,130 px · 34 nodes Scale in a 1,100 × 560 frame 0.26

.lc4-frame { height: clamp(480px, 78vh, 900px); }
<likec4-view view-id="v5_frame" browser></likec4-view>

For documents and slides, likec4 export png --max-width 4000 project renders any size at full resolution; the ASD and Zensical pages use that export, not a screenshot of the frame.
